summary:
Developed by Team Dark Horse, the Planetary Similarity Ranking System (PSRS) and Lunar Base Similarity Ranking System (LB-SRS) form a data-driven Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) framework evaluating 75 terrestrial analog testbeds across 5 major Martian and lunar regions. Using a dual-index model combining the Weighted Sum Model (WSM) and Physical Similarity Index (PSI/L-PSI), the system bridges the physical gap between Earth environments and space realities. By integrating open-source datasets from NASA (including LRO LOLA, MRO CRISM, and JPL EMIT), ISRO, and ESA, our framework successfully matches strategic landing sites—such as Jezero Crater, Shackleton Crater, and Marius Hills—with high-fidelity Earth counterparts like Lake Salda and the McMurdo Dry Valleys.
       This project is vital because it provides researchers with a rigorous, algorithmically robust tool to validate rover mobility, ISRU extraction, and habitat designs on Earth prior to costly space missions, directly supporting Artemis and future planetary exploration.
details:
Project Summary & Overview

Planetary & Lunar Similarity Ranking Systems (PSRS & LB-SRS) is an advanced, data-driven Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) web platform developed by Team Dark Horse to bridge the physics gap between Earth and extraterrestrial environments. Our project maps and ranks terrestrial geological analogs across the globe to match specific landing sites, exploration targets, and permanent base locations on the Moon (LB-SRS) and Mars (PSRS).

How It Works & Core Architecture

The platform implements a robust dual-index scoring model:

  1. WSM (Mission Readiness Index): Evaluates operational access, field logistics, permits, and deployment feasibility alongside scientific fidelity.
  2. PSI / L-PSI (Physical Similarity Index): Isolates pure geological, mineralogical, and atmospheric parameters (such as basaltic composition, analog soil mechanics, and UV/radiation exposure) to find the closest natural Earth counterparts.
  3. Algorithmic Robustness: Validated via ±5% weight perturbation sensitivity testing, which proved 100% Top-1 stability across all target sites

Key Features & Mapped Analogs

  • Mars Analogs (PSRS): Connects Martian sites like Jezero Crater to Lake Salda (Turkey), Gale Crater to Salar de Atacama (Chile), and Olympus Mons to Mauna Kea (Hawaii).
  • Lunar Analogs (LB-SRS): Identifies specialized testbeds for Artemis & LUPEX missions, pairing Shackleton Crater Rim with the McMurdo Dry Valleys, Marius Hills with Spanish volcanic lava tubes, and lunar highland anorthosites with Sittampundi (Tamil Nadu).
  • Interactive Web Portal & Reports: Fully deployed and accessible via our project web portal, complete with downloadable comprehensive technical reports and datasets.

Intended Impact & Benefits

By rigorously quantifying how well Earth testbeds mimic extraterrestrial conditions, PSRS & LB-SRS dramatically reduce mission risks, optimize rover mobility trials, and streamline analog astronaut training. It provides space agencies and researchers with an objective, multi-criteria decision tool to select the most cost-effective and physically accurate terrestrial testing grounds.

Development Tools & Technologies

  • Programming & Logic: Python, Data-driven MCDA algorithms.
  • Data Sources: NASA LRO (LOLA/LAMP), ISRO (Chandrayaan-2/3), JAXA (SELENE), USGS, and ESA Copernicus datasets.
  • Deployment & Presentation: Web hosting via Vercel, interactive mapping interfaces, and structured technical documentation.
